read.title: Iterative finite element approximation of non-monotone semilinear diffusion-reaction equations

results.statement: Experiment 1 (general case): for the non-monotone semilinear problem with the re-entrant corner solution (6.3), the iterative linearized Galerkin solutions u_N on graded meshes are expected, by Rmk. 7 / estimate (5.6), to converge (up to a subsequence) at the optimal rate (4.1). The H1/energy-type error is observed to decay like dim(V_N)^(-1/2).
results.norm: H1 / energy norm (norm (2.1) with λ = 1, the global error against the exact solution)
results.rate_formula: ||u - u_N|| ~ dim(V_N)^(-1/2), i.e. the optimal rate (4.1), for a subsequence
results.assumptions: Scalar semilinear elliptic problem -Δu = f(x,u) + g with homogeneous Dirichlet data on a 2D domain with a re-entrant corner at c1 = (0,0). f satisfies Asm. 2.1 (uniformly bounded derivative f_u), and in the general case f_u must be continuous in u (Thm. 4.10). The time step satisfies Asm. 3.1. The IMEX iteration (3.7) runs until the slope between two meshes is < -0.49, or up to the iteration cap (6.2) with γ = 1. Meshes are graded toward the corner through RGB refinement with grading parameter β = 0.4 > 1/3 (defined in §4.1, which is not in the passage), with h from 0.25 down to 0.0019. The polynomial degree is not stated in the passage; the rate dim(V_N)^(-1/2) suggests P1 (linear) elements. Exp. 3 shows the optimal rate fails when f_u is discontinuous and ρ > 1/C_P.
results.regularity: u ∈ H^1_0 (a weak solution) with a re-entrant corner singularity at (0,0). The exact regularity class and singular exponent of (6.3) are not in the passage. Grading is used to restore the optimal rate.
results.quote: By Rmk. 7 (see, in particular, the estimate (5.6)), we expect the sequence {uN }N ≥0 to converge (up to a subsequence) at optimal rate (4.1).

results.statement: Experiment 2 (special, contractive case): when α < ρ ≤ 1/C_P, the reduced scheme (3.8) with Δt = ∞ produces the whole sequence u_N, which reaches the optimal convergence rate on the same graded meshes. Continuity of f_u is not needed here.
results.rate_formula: optimal rate (4.1), observed as the same rate as Exp. 6.1, dim(V_N)^(-1/2)
results.assumptions: Same domain, exact solution (6.3) and graded meshes (β = 0.4) as Exp. 1. f satisfies Asm. 2.1 with ρ ≤ 1/C_P (special case, contraction), and f_u may be discontinuous. Asm. 3.1 holds automatically. Uses scheme (3.8), α = 9.6 and γ = 1. The degree is not stated (P1 is implied by the rate).
results.regularity: Same corner-singular weak solution as Exp. 1. The reaction term f is Lipschitz with a discontinuous derivative.
results.quote: As a result, Rmk. 7(ii) ensures {uN }N ≥0 reaches the optimal rate of convergence.

results.statement: General qualitative a-priori result (Conclusions): the Galerkin limits converge weakly to a weak solution of (1.1), and a subsequence converges strongly. In the contractive special case the whole sequence converges. No rate is given.
results.norm: weak convergence and strong convergence in V (H1-type norm)
results.rate_formula: no rate: convergence only (weak convergence; strong convergence for a subsequence; full sequence in the contractive case)
results.assumptions: Semilinear elliptic problems (1.1) with non-monotone reaction terms whose derivative is uniformly bounded, solved with the IMEX-FEM iterative linearized Galerkin scheme. The mesh and polynomial-degree conditions are not stated in the passage.
results.regularity: Only a weak solution in V (H^1_0) is required.
results.quote: we have demonstrated weak convergence of the Galerkin limits to a weak solution of (1.1), and we have established strong convergence for a subsequence.
